chapter: Apollo Bar, Apollo managers and Harlem nightlife
title: Unpaid at the gangster-run Cat's Meow
summary: At the Cat's Meow in Brooklyn the owner owed him a week's pay, hit him in the office, and Whaley told the band not to play.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I remember over at the Cat's Meow in Brooklyn, the gangsters run that place and they had a show, chorus girls and everything and the man owed me money for a week and he said he's going to give to me when I open up but he didn't give it to me so I wouldn't play there, no, you got to give us some money. We don't play. He took me in
the office and he hit me. I said I know you ain't going to get no more music now.
So I told the band don't play nothing.
